title: content/board/board.json
description: M7-05 — the loc keys the Board screen (S05) renders. What is fixed here is that the screen labels HP, Gold, the stage, the number last rolled and the tile it stands on; offers a roll, a tile acknowledgement and the two fork branches; carries one status line per state the read can be in and one per reason a roll is refused; and names all fifteen tile kinds. Every value is a loc key, so the content build resolves it against every locale file: a key this document names but a locale does not carry fails the build, and a locale string this document stops naming fails it as an orphan. additionalProperties is false on every object so the absences are enforced rather than merely observed. The `forkLabel` group is what that absence turned into: BoardView.Project exports the bias label each branch's tiles were actually drawn under, so the four labels are named here and the two branch buttons say where they go. The `dice` group is the fixed dice (`04` §6) — a tray heading, and the prompt asking the player to name a granted die's number. Neither group carries a numeral: a die's number and a fork branch's icons are drawn from values the run and the board already carry, and a number needs no translation.

locKey.description: loc.<domain>.<id>.<field>, lowercase, dot-separated, snake_case segments — the same shape schema/loc.schema.json governs the locale files by.

label.description: The captions beside the values the run row literally carries. HP and Gold are on the run; the stage is derived from the run's pending tile against the chapter's own stage list; 'rolled' captions the number the last accepted roll came up, and 'standing on' the tile that has not been resolved yet.

gate.description: 🔴 What the mark on a barred node MEANS, in words, under the track. Required, and required from this screen in particular: a node a move may not carry past is drawn as a shape, and a shape on a screen with no icon set, no legend and no tooltip is a rule the player can see and cannot read — so a roll of 5 that moves 2 reads as a cheat rather than as a rule. The shape says which node; this says what it does, and it is on screen BEFORE the rule costs anything rather than arriving with the stop. It also states the one thing no mark can: nothing skips the fight, an armed escape included.

action.description: Every control the screen offers. The two fork captions are separate keys rather than one parameterised caption because they are the run's one real navigation decision and a player choosing between two identical words has not chosen anything.

skipUnbuilt.description: 🔴 What the tile control reads on a tile whose own screen this build has not written — an Event or a Minigame. A second key rather than a reused `resolve`, because it is a different offer: `Continue` promises the screen the tile is supposed to open, and the press actually resolves the tile WITHOUT one. Required rather than optional so that deleting the placeholder is a diff somebody has to argue for, the same way `abandonConfirm` is required.

abandon.description: The control that gives up the run. Required, and required from THIS screen in particular: 16 D39 makes ABANDON_RUN legal from every state a live run can stand in, and this is the only surface that reaches it — a board standing on a tile whose screen this build has not written has no other way out.

abandonConfirm.description: What the same control reads once armed. A second key rather than a reused one: abandoning is unrecoverable and pays a tenth of what the run banked, so the confirmation has to STATE that rather than repeat the offer the player already pressed.

forkLabel.description: 03 §3.1's four fork-branch bias labels, one key each. Exported by BoardView as ForkLabel and drawn on the branch button beside the branch's own first tiles — so the label and the icons are two independent reads of the same branch rather than one derived from the other. Four separate keys rather than one parameterised caption, for the reason the two branch actions are separate: a player choosing between two identical words has not chosen anything.

dice.description: The fixed dice (`04` §6). `held` captions the tray of dice the run owns, each drawn as its own number; `choose` is the prompt a granted die opens, because the player names the number rather than being given one. 🔒 Neither key carries the number itself, and no key here is parameterised on a count: a numeral is drawn from the run's own state and translating one would be inventing a plural rule for a value that has none.

name.description: The fork prompt's heading. A heading rather than a status line, because a junction is a question the screen is asking rather than a state it is reporting.

status.description: The line shown while the screen has no board to act on, plus the line about an action that was refused. 'refused' covers every rejection the rules layer can answer with. There used to be a second, 'rerollExhausted', separated because the reroll cap arrived as its own wire value; it is gone with the reroll.

block.description: 🔒 One sentence per reason the roll is not live, and the reason this object exists at all: a tile left unresolved, a fork left unchosen, a battle left unfought and a draft left untaken all refuse a roll with the SAME wire value. A screen that showed one sentence for all four would tell the player the roll failed and not one thing they could do about it — and each of the four is escaped by doing something different. The screen therefore decides the cause from the run's own state before submitting anything, and these are the sentences it can then say.

unbuiltScreen.description: 🔴 A FIFTH sentence, and the only one that admits a gap in the build rather than naming a state of the run. Two of the fifteen tile kinds — Event and Minigame — are left by a command only their own screen submits, and neither screen exists, so `tile`'s `resolve this tile before rolling again` told a player standing on one to do something no control on the screen could do. This says the screen is missing and what the skip does instead.

gate.description: 🔴 A SIXTH sentence, and the one read at the moment the rule has already cost something. `tile` — `resolve this tile before rolling again` — is true of a mini-boss node and explains neither why the move stopped short of the number rolled nor why an armed escape did not fire, and this is the only place on the screen where either can be said where it happened.

tile.description: All fifteen tile kinds by name. Required in full rather than as an open map: the run reports the tile it stands on as a bare integer, the enum that gives that integer a name is internal to the rules, and the client's own integer-to-name table is therefore a transcription. Requiring every member here is what makes a kind added to the game fail this document rather than render as a number.
